newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina seeks Mercosur import financing deal.
newsitem.headline: Argentina seeks Mercosur import financing deal.

text.p: Argentina Thursday sought to play down its trade dispute with Brazil and said it will push for a common policy on import financing within the Mercosur customs union.

"We have to iron out some differences and that is what these kinds of meetings are for," President Carlos Menem told reporters of talks he plans this weekend with Brazilian leader Fernando Henrique Cardoso in Rio de Janeiro.
He called Brazil's decision to put a cap on import financing "a drastic measure" which could result in trade restrictions, but trusted the differences could be solved through dialogue.

Economy Minister Roque Fernandez told a separate news conference that Argentina wanted its partners in Mercosur -- Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay -- to adopt a common regime for financing imports by July 31. He added group members would seek to have a blueprint ready for the Mercosur presidential meeting due next June in Asuncion, Paraguay.
Brazil angered its Mercosur partners earlier this month by slapping limits on import financing on loans under 360 days in duration, effectively forcing Brazilian importers to pay cash.
Paraguay called an urgent meeting of Mercosur finance chiefs earlier this week to discuss the issue but no clear agreements resulted from the talks.

The Mercosur Inter-Parliamentary Committee urged economy chiefs in Asuncion to come up with "a mechanism that ensures previous consultation before the adoption of economic measures by every state that could affect its partners."
Fernandez said Argentine sugar, cotton and rice were some of the export items more vulnerable to Brazil's move.
